evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Schweiz: Helvetia
terms.comment: Named after the Helvētiī, the people Caesar fought (BG 1); the adjective is Helvētius, Swiss. A country takes a preposition: in Helvētiam (to), in Helvētiā (in), ex Helvētiā (from).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 389.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
